title: introduce-rag-traffic-fuzzer-and-step-assertions-quickstart
author: Maya Liu
description: Summary: Adds a new quickstart that demonstrates a lightweight traffic fuzzer and a stepwise assertion DSL for RAG workloads, designed for local devloops and CI smoke tests; Motivation: teams building retrieval-augmented agents need reproducible, high-variance traffic to validate retrieval correctness, tool-calling flows, and quality regressions across model variants; What this PR introduces: 1) quickstarts/rag-traffic-fuzzer/ -- a self-contained playground with a composable traffic generator that emits conversational sequences with configurable retrieval jitter, latency simulation, and tool call injection; 2) an assertions/step-assertions.py DSL that lets authors write step-by-step expectations against agent traces (retrieval hits, tool inputs, tool responses, and output assertions); 3) three example scenarios (simple FAQ rerank, multi-tool booking flow, and degraded-retrieval-fallback) demonstrating common regressions and canary checks; 4) a local devloop entry script and a Dockerdev image for reproducible environment; 5) docs site metadata to surface the quickstart under "Testing & Quickstarts"; Compatibility: works with hosted and dedicated Redwood endpoints and includes a lightweight adapter for the OpenAI-compatible API surface; Usage: run scripts/setup-devloop.sh to bootstrap, then `./devloop run --scenario simple-scenario` to generate traffic and assert expectations; Contribution notes: includes checklist for maintainers to add new scenarios, guidance for perf-sensitive CI (sample smoke workflow), and a small notebook for manual exploration; Security & data: scenarios use synthetic fixtures only and include guidance for swapping in customer indexes safely; Tests & CI: added a smoke workflow that runs the sample scenario against the dev Docker image and validates that assertions pass; Rollout: feature flagged behind docs metadata and ready to ship as a community quickstart; See commits and changed_files for details.
commits: Initial scaffold: add traffic-fuzzer tool, README and three example scenarios
Add step-assertion DSL, test harness and example assertions
Add Dockerdev image and setup script; update README with run instructions
Fix CI flake: pin pytest timeout and add retry for transient network check
Docs: register quickstart in site metadata and add cross-links to RAG best-practices
review_comments: Evan Cho: Nice ergonomics on the DSL, can we make the assertion failure messages more actionable (include retrieval hit score and matched doc id)?; Author reply: Added score/id in the latest commit and included an example output in the README.

Priya Nair: The CI job flaked once in my run; please add a small retry around the ephemeral container pull step.; Author reply: Added a 3-attempt retry and exponential backoff to ci/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml and bumped timeout.

Samir Patel: For Dedicated customers the latency simulation needs a note about not injecting into production traffic; Author reply: Added a security note and a feature flag comment so the traffic generator defaults to offline/synthetic indexes only.

Evan Cho: Can we have a tiny TypeScript wrapper example for teams using the TS SDK?; Author reply: Added a short example snippet to the README showing TS SDK usage and link to redwood-sdk-typescript examples.
approvals: Priya Nair: approved after CI fix
release_notes: Add a new RAG quickstart: 'rag-traffic-fuzzer' offering a configurable traffic generator and stepwise assertion DSL for reproducible RAG testing; Includes three example scenarios (FAQ rerank, booking multi-tool flow, degraded-retrieval fallback), Dockerdev image and CI smoke workflow; Exposes guidance for swapping synthetic fixtures with customer indexes; Suggested next steps: add language-specific wrappers and integrate into the quickstart smoke matrix.
